extracted.intended_audience: students, faculty, and library users seeking reliable fact-checking resources
extracted.subtask_description: A college library research guide listing reputable fact‑checking websites and describing the principles, missions, and practices that make those sites useful for verifying information. Use this to identify trustworthy fact checks and understand different fact‑checking approaches (e.g., general, scientific, bias-rating, educational).

rubrics_metrics.name: PolitiFact core principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact-checking journalism is the heart of PolitiFact. Our core principles are independence, transparency, fairness, thorough reporting and clear writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: to give citizens the information they need to govern themselves in a democracy. Emphasizes independence, transparent methods, fair treatment of claims, rigorous reporting, and readable presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpartisan, nonprofit consumer‑advocate approach (FactCheck.org)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are a nonpartisan, nonprofit 'consumer advocate' for voters that aims to reduce the level of deception and confusion in U.S. politics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitors factual accuracy of TV ads, debates, speeches, interviews and news releases; aims to apply best practices of both journalism and scholarship and to increase public knowledge and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credentialed journalistic expertise (Washington Post Fact Checker)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fact Checker is led by experienced, beat‑knowledgeable journalists (example: Glenn Kessler's decades of reporting across foreign policy, economic policy, White House, Congress, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied criterion: fact-checking led by journalists with relevant reporting experience and subject-matter familiarity enhances credibility and depth of analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document sources and evidence-based investigative reporting (Snopes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes.com’s fact checking and original, investigative reporting lights the way to evidence-based and contextualized analysis. We always document our sources so readers are empowered to do independent research and make up their own minds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes documenting sources, contextualizing claims, and using original investigative work to trace and verify rumors, urban legends, and contemporary misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-oriented fact-checking and academic oversight (Duke Reporters’ Lab)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reporters’ Lab is a center for journalism research... Our core projects focus on fact-checking, but we also do occasional research about trust in the news media and other topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: fact‑checking efforts informed by academic research centers contribute methodological rigor, tracking, and meta‑study of fact-checking practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-specialized fact-checking (SciCheck)
rubrics_metrics.description: FactCheck.org’s SciCheck feature focuses exclusively on false and misleading scientific claims that are made by partisans to influence public policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialization (e.g., scientific claims) is a deliberate editorial choice to apply domain expertise and tailored methods to a class of claims; such verticals may be grant-funded and designed for depth over breadth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational media‑literacy resources and argument analysis (FlackCheck)
rubrics_metrics.description: FlackCheck.org provides resources designed to help viewers recognize flaws in arguments in general and political ads in particular. Video resources point out deception and incivility in political rhetoric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: providing teachable resources (videos, guides) that explain rhetorical flaws and deceptive techniques supports public media literacy alongside direct fact checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit methodology for bias assessment and funding transparency (Media Bias/Fact Check)
rubrics_metrics.description: MBFC follows a strict methodology for determining the biases of sources... Funding for Media Bias Fact Check comes from donations and third-party advertising. We use third-party advertising to prevent influence and bias... Ads are generated based on your search history, cookies, and the content of the current web page you are viewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative criteria: publish and follow a clear methodology for bias ratings; disclose funding and advertising practices and note how those practices can nonetheless produce ad-related bias or perception of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional independence, nonprofit mission, and networked reach (NPR FactCheck)
rubrics_metrics.description: NPR is an independent, nonprofit media organization... founded on a mission to create a more informed public. Through its network of member stations, NPR makes local stories national, national stories local, and global stories personal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: nonprofit status, stated public‑service mission, and broad distributed network lend editorial independence, reach, and contextual reporting capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of checklists and stepwise evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: This guide links to resources such as 'How to Spot Fake News- a checklist' and '5 Steps to Evaluating Web Sites'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: complement relying on fact-check sites with user-focused checklists and stepwise evaluation methods to assess sources, claims, and web content directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage across formats and venues
rubrics_metrics.description: FactCheck.org monitors the factual accuracy of what is said by major U.S. political players in the form of TV ads, debates, speeches, interviews and news releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: trustworthy fact-checking examines claims across multiple formats (ads, debates, speeches, interviews, press releases) rather than only written web posts, because misinformation appears in many venues.
